quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What may help if your drive chain slips?
questions.explanation: If your chain slips, try tightening it. If this does not fix the problem, replace the chain before riding again.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about dangers or changes in road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what does it mean when the lead rider raises their left arm and extends their index finger?

options.text: The group will exit at the next exit

questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider raises their left arm and extends their index finger, it means all riders should form a single-file line.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, you should:

options.text: Always ride in the center of the lane
Always ride on the left side of the lane
Always ride on the right side of the lane
Change your position based on different conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your position based on different conditions
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Choose where you are most visible to others and can keep safe space around you.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: The greatest risk of conflict happens at intersections. Stay alert for vehicles that might cross your path.

questions.question: To ride safely on slippery surfaces, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Avoid the center of the lane when the road is wet

questions.explanation: To ride safely on slippery surfaces, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes when needed. Watch for oil, dirt, gravel, and wet or frozen areas.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Is the best way to know they see you
Does not guarantee they will yield to you
Guarantees they will yield to you

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee they will yield to you
questions.explanation: Do not assume eye contact means a driver will yield. Drivers often look at a motorcycle but fail to see it.

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield must be all of the following, except:

options.text: Too tight to wear sunglasses or eyeglasses

questions.correctAnswerText: Too tight to wear sunglasses or eyeglasses
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must fasten securely, be scratch-free, allow clear side vision, resist damage, permit airflow to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: It is a good idea to wear reflective clothing:
questions.explanation: Wear bright and reflective clothing whenever you ride. Crashes happen both day and night, so stay visible at all times.

questions.question: A passenger should never:
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear helmets and eye protection. Passengers must avoid loose clothing that could catch on the motorcycle. They must lean with the operator during turns. Passengers must never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: A major effect of alcohol is:
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down both physical and mental functions.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Sit so you use your arms to steer, not to support yourself.
Sit far back so you can keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you use your arms to steer, not to support yourself.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests to maintain balance.

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield should have all of these features, except:
questions.explanation: Good eye protection and face shields must be free of scratches, resist breaking, have a clear side view, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and fit over eyeglasses or sunglasses.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing helps others see you in all conditions. Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day, so wear bright clothing at all times.

questions.question: Which is not protective riding gear?
questions.explanation: Proper protective gear includes a jacket and pants made of leather or sturdy material, boots that cover and support your ankles, and hearing protection even with a helmet.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handlegrip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever usually located?
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handlegrip. Know where all your controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Provides less than half the braking power.
Provides about 70 percent of the braking power.
Should only be used on wet roads.
Should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides about 70 percent of the braking power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much stronger than the rear brake and provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which protects your eyes from the wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake right away and then apply it smoothly again.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and let the motorcycle coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and then apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks up while braking, release the front brake immediately and re-apply it smoothly.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should motorcyclists do about space?

options.text: Do not need extra space around them.
Should cut their normal space cushion in half.
Should keep enough space around each rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should keep enough space around each rider.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, keep close together but still maintain enough space cushion around each rider.

questions.question: Which action will NOT help prevent a friend from driving while drunk?

options.text: Arrange safe transportation home for them.
Keep them busy with activities to slow their drinking and help them sober up.
Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
Ask other friends to help stop them from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
questions.explanation: To prevent drunk driving, arrange another way home, keep them busy with activities, find excuses to keep them from leaving, and ask friends to help. Waiting 15 minutes after drinking does not prevent drunk driving.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They are caused by worn-out tires.
They occur at speeds above 55 mph.
They involve new or inexperienced riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve new or inexperienced riders.
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience. Most crashes happen during the day at low speeds.

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.explanation: Wear gear that makes you and your motorcycle easier to spot. Bright, reflective clothing helps other drivers see you better.
